# dsh-preclaim
> **Repository name vs package name:** the repo is `dsh-evidence`; the npm package is `dsh-preclaim`
. They are the same plugin.

**A commit message that says "tests pass" is a claim. This checks it against what
the session actual
ly ran — and stops the commit if the two disagree.**

A DeepSeek Harness plugin.
No model, no service, no network, no API key.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> **Why `preclaim` and not `evidence-gate`?** Because the obvious names are held by
> other authors,

some of them for plugins asking the same question:
> `dsh-evidence-gate` (lory.top), `dsh-evidence`

(tudamu), `dsh-claim-gate`,
> `dsh-attest`. The project's design document checked the registry and

picked the
> free name that describes the right moment: **before the claim is written down.**
> `scr

ipts/verify-artifacts.mjs` fails the build if a later edit drifts back onto a
> name somebody else o

/verify-artifacts.mjs` fails the build if a later edit drifts back onto a
> name somebody else owns.
## Why this exists, and why it is not a model

The failure it targets is not a judgement call. "The message claims tests pass"
and "no test run is

recorded in this session" are both facts, and whether they
agree is decidable. A model here would ad

d a confidence interval to a yes/no
question, and would occasionally be wrong in a way nobody could

ence interval to a yes/no
question, and would occasionally be wrong in a way nobody could reproduce.
So the whole plugin is deterministic:

* **`tools/post-execute` records what ran** into an in-memory ledger for the
session.
* **`tools/pre
-execute` reads that ledger** before a gated action runs.

Three consequences follow from that split, and they are the design rather than
implementation detail

ree consequences follow from that split, and they are the design rather than
implementation details:

1. **A claim cannot satisfy its own obligation.** The action under review is never
consulted for evi

dence. A commit message saying "ran pytest; all tests pass"
contributes nothing to its own check.
2.

**A failed test run does not count as evidence that tests pass.** `test-run` and
`build-run` requir

e success. `ci-check` and `file-read` do not: observing a red
pipeline is still observing the pipeli

ne, and reading a file is evidence of
reading it whatever the exit code.
3. **Nothing is inferred fr

om prose.** The ledger holds what the host reported, and
nothing else. There is no transcript readin
g and no heuristic scanning.
## What is gated

**Shell calls** running an asserting git verb — `commit`, `push`, `tag`. A commit
carries its messag

e inline; a push asserts through the commits it carries, so the
command text is checked and the comm
it range is left to the human.

Read-only verbs (`status`, `log`, `diff`, `show`, `branch`, `rev-parse`, …) are
never gated, and nei

ther are `--dry-run`, `--help`, `-h` or `--version`: none of
those makes a durable claim. `git fetch

&& git commit -m x` gates the commit and
not the fetch.

**README-shaped writes** — `README*`, `CHANGELOG*`, `docs/**/*.md`, `**/README.md`.
A README is wher

e a project states what it does and whether it works. Ordinary
source writes are left alone; gating

those would put a gate in front of every edit.
A write outside the working directory is not judged a

would put a gate in front of every edit.
A write outside the working directory is not judged at all.
## What counts as a claim
| pattern | what it notices | answered by |

| `CLAIM_TEST_PASSED` | says tests pass | a recorded test run |
| `CLAIM_VERIFIED` | says something

was verified | **nothing observable** → `tool_unverified` |
| `CLAIM_RAN_CHECK` | says a check was r

un | a recorded test run |
| `CLAIM_BUILD_OK` | says the build succeeds | a recorded build |
| `CLAI

M_CLI_ASSERTION` | names a CLI invocation | a CI observation |
| `CLAIM_DEPENDENCY` | asserts a plat

form dependency | **nothing observable** → `tool_unverified` |
| `CLAIM_LINE_REF` | cites a line | a

file read |
| `CLAIM_COUNT` | cites a count | **nothing observable** → `tool_unverified` |
| `CLAIM

_HASH_REF` | cites a commit hash | **nothing observable** → `tool_unverified` |
| `CLAIM_FILE_EXISTS
` | cites a file | a file read |

The last column has a rule behind it: **evidence has to connect to the claim it
answers.** `file-rea

d` answers a citation of a file or a line, because reading that
file *is* the connection. It does **

not** answer "this was verified" — reading
*some* file is not verifying *that* claim. An earlier ver

sion treated it as if it
were, which made `git commit -m "verified on Windows"` pass as soon as anyt

hing at
all had been read.

The four kinds mapping to nothing are not an oversight. They are claims this gate
can observe but ca

nnot adjudicate, so it says so and asks
(`tool_unverified`) rather than making an accusation it cann

cate, so it says so and asks
(`tool_unverified`) rather than making an accusation it cannot support.

If no pattern matches, the action is allowed with `no-claim-in-action`. The patterns
are deliberatel

y syntactic: a wider net means more false stops on honest work, and a
gate that cries wolf gets swit
ched off — after which it checks nothing at all.
## What happens on a miss
| situation | verdict | why |

| not a watched action | `allow` | nothing to check |
| a watched action carrying no claim | `allow`

| still nothing to check |
| every claim backed by recorded evidence | `allow` | the claim and the

record agree |
| a claim with no evidence, ledger populated | `review` | the claim is not backed |
|
**the ledger is empty** | `review`, and says so | cannot distinguish "it did not happen" from "I di

d not see it" |
| a claim no observable evidence could answer | `review` (`tool_unverified`) | a lim

it of this gate, not an accusation |
| the gate itself throws | `review` | a defect must not become

not an accusation |
| the gate itself throws | `review` | a defect must not become a silent allow |
Two of those rows are worth reading twice.

**The empty ledger** happens whenever the plugin loads mid-session, or when
recording failed. Report

ing "the tests did not run" in that state would be a
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements

Node `^22.19.0 || >=24.0.0`. No runtime dependencies. `@deepseek-ai/cordis` is an
optional peer.
